#### Liquids Tab

The Liquids tab contains general setup information for liquid meters.

This feature is only available with the **FLOWCAL Liquids** module.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 589;height: 550;" />

<span id="Setup"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Setup">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Setup Sub-Tab</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Setup">

Use this tab to specify products that should flow on a meter, the tolerance window at the end of a batch for finding a matching sample, and other options specific to liquid meters.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Batch Options">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Batch Options</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="background-color: #ffffff; display: none;" mc-target-name="Batch Options">

- **Operation Type**\*
  - **Batch** - Default option for liquid meters. When operating in this mode, a meter allows for input of both batch and periodic data. When batch data is entered or imported, the flow data is broken down and distributed to each of the periodic records that fall within its duration. When periodic data is provided, the values of a record are aggregated with the other periodic records that fall within a batch to determine the batch total.

  - **Run Ticket** - For meters with intermittent flow such as truck or rail car loading or unloading. When operating in this mode, flow data may only be entered under the periodic tab in the Volume Editor. All records created in this manner are restricted to one second in duration. Records may be created under the Batch tab, but only the start and end dates may be specified; these records behave purely as a container for the underlying periodic records.

    Run Ticket essentially allows users to enter meter data that imitates tickets.

<!-- -->

- **Create Batch on New Analysis** - This option enables automatically creates a new batch upon a new analysis being manually created or imported to this meter.
- **Create Batch on Off Hour Record** - This option splits a batch if a periodic record is imported with an effective date that does not fall at the meter’s specified data resolution as defined in the meter characteristics in the Volume Editor. For instance, if a meter is set up with daily data resolution and it has a contract hour of seven, any record that comes in with a time that is not at 07:00:00 would cause a batch split. If a meter is set up with hourly data resolution, any record that comes in with a time not at the top of the hour would cause a batch split.
- <span id="Reconcile"></span>**Reconcile Batches**\* - Enables the Batch Movement Reconciliation functionality. When enabled, meter batches must be scheduled (See Batch Movement Reconciliation). As the actual batches import, if they cannot be matched to a scheduled batch, exceptions will be generated to alert the user to this.

**\*** Not available for dead oil meters.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Sample Tolerances">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Sample Tolerances</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="background-color: #ffffff; display: none;" mc-target-name="Sample Tolerances">

**Before/After End of Batch** - When a Liquid Quality Source Assignment is created using the option to apply samples at the end of a batch, the default behavior is such that a sample can only be applied to a batch if its sample date falls on the exact second that the batch ends. The Sample Tolerance settings allow a user to specify a window around the end of a batch for which a sample will be considered applicable. The maximum for both Before and End of Batch options is 365 days.

If multiple samples are within the window, the last one is used. If no window is given, then a sample would only be applied to a batch if one of the following is true:

- The assignment is set up to use effective date and time and a sample with a corresponding sample date exists.
- The assignment is end of batch and the batch’s end date and time matches the sample’s date and time.
- The assignment is end of batch and the Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited option is checked.

An option to use the first sample found is available in the [Quality Assignment Editor](../../Source%20Analysis/Quality%20Assignment%20Editor/Configuring%20Assignments.md) screen.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Import Options">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Import Options</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="background-color: #ffffff; display: none;" mc-target-name="Import Options">

This group of options is not available for dead oil meters.

- **Apply Last Edited/Imported MF to the Batch** - When a new meter factor is imported or edited, FLOWCAL splits the meter characteristic record and applies the new meter factor at the effective date of the history record or the event and uses the new meter factor from that point forward. It may be desirable to have FLOWCAL apply the value back to the start of the batch.

  Checking this option causes FLOWCAL to update the meter factor back to the start of the current batch with the new value. Volume, mass, component volume and component mass values are recalculated for the time period the meter factor is applied to. New revisions for the meter characteristics record, the periodic data and the batch are created. An edit reason of “New MF Applied to Start of Batch” is created as well.

  If unchecked, then the meter factor at the date of the change is used.

- **Apply Last Edited/Imported DMF to the Batch** - This option is the same as the Apply Last Edited/Imported MF to the Batch option, except it is applicable to the DMF.

- **Recalc Method** - Determines the recalculation method to use when applying import options.

FLOWCAL does not apply a MF or DMF of 0 as it does not consider a MF or DMF of 0 to be a valid value to apply to the batch. If the last edited or imported MF or DMF is 0, then FLOWCAL looks to the prior MF or DMF within the batch and applies that value to the whole batch. The MF and DMF are considered separately during the apply process.

</div>

<span id="ValidateProducts"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Validate">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Validate Products</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="background-color: #ffffff; display: none;" mc-target-name="Validate">

- **Validate Products -** When the option to Validate Products is selected, the product drop-down in the Volume Editor will show only the products specified on this tab; no other products may be selected. On import, if a product not in the list of valid products is imported, an exception will be generated.

- **Add/Edit Product** - Add or edit a product.

  Clicking the Add or Edit Product buttons will open the Configure Product screen. The base density and base density unit are automatically populated by the values specified in the Product Editor if available, but with the exception of products assigned a table type that has a fixed base density, these values can be edited.

  If the Always Use Base Conditions as Observed option is checked, the base density specified for the product in the Validate Products section of the Meter Editor and the base temperature specified in the Product Editor will replace the observed density and temperature of a record on import. Unit conversion between the density from the units specified in the Meter Editor and the units found in meter characteristics will be done.

  The Sample Required checkbox enables a validation when a liquid source is assigned to a meter that requires each record on that meter to be associated with a sample analysis. If a record does not have a sample applied to it, an exception will be generated.

- **Remove Product** - Remove a product.

  Once removed, unless the Validate Products checkbox is unchecked, the product will no longer appear on the Product drop-down of the Volume Editor for the meter.

  Any records that have already been saved with that product will retain their product information; however, and an edit made to these records will generate an exception. Likewise, if a file is imported with invalid products, the records will still be saved, but an exception will be generated.

- **Set as Default** - The selected product will become the meter's default product. When a new batch record is created, this product will automatically be selected, if there is not already a product on the record. The product can be changed to any other valid product specified for the meter, so this is a matter of convenience.

  A default product will not populate when entering edit mode from the Periodic tab for both Flow Data and Characteristic records.

</div>

</div>

<span id="Schedules"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Schedules">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Schedules Sub-Tab</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Schedules">

Batch schedules can be assigned to a meter to automatically create batches for liquid meters that deliver batches on a known schedule, with known products. You can assign a different batch schedule for a meter on a month-by-month basis if the product flow or the day of the month that the batch starts on changes.

The use of a batch schedule can be helpful if batches are to be hand-keyed into the system, or if the import file doesn’t contain the batch start and stop or the batch product information. When batches are created from a schedule, each batch starts and ends at the contract hour set in meter characteristics on the day specified in the schedule.

Monthly batch schedules are created from the [Batch Schedule Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Liquids/Batch%20Schedule%20Editor.md) and annual schedules are created from the [Annual Schedule Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/Annual%20Schedule%20Editor.md).

For FLOWCAL to create batches based on a batch schedule, the service FcBatchScheduler.exe must be installed and running.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 561;height: 522;" />

If the service FcBatchScheduler.exe runs, but cannot create batches on a meter because it is locked by another process such as meter rollups or a user performing edits, no messages will be generated. FcBatchScheduler should be run during off hours to minimize the chances of this happening and to minimize database access during peak hours.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Monthly Schedule">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Monthly Schedule</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="background-color: #ffffff; display: none;" mc-target-name="Monthly Schedule">

<div class="procedure">

To select a monthly schedule:

1.  Within the Meter Editor, select a meter and click **Edit**.
2.  Select the Monthly Schedule option and click on the button to the right. The Batch Schedule Select screen will display.
3.  Select the schedule from the drop-down and click **Select**.
4.  Click **Save**.

To delete a monthly schedule:

1.  Within the Meter Editor, select a meter and click **Edit**.
2.  Click the button with the red circle and minus sign in the Regular Schedule section.
3.  Click **Save**.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Annual Schedule">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Annual Schedule</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="background-color: #ffffff; display: none;" mc-target-name="Annual Schedule">

<div class="procedure">

To select an annual schedule:

1.  Within the Meter Editor, select a meter and click **Edit**.
2.  Select the Annual Schedule option and click on the button to the right of the Monthly Schedule label. The Annual Schedule Editor screen will display.
3.  Choose the schedule from the drop-down and click **Apply**.
4.  Click **Save**.

To delete an annual schedule:

1.  Within the Meter Editor, select a meter and click **Edit**.
2.  Click the button with the red circle and minus sign in the Regular Schedule section.
3.  Click **Save**.

</div>

Unlike a monthly batch schedule, no product is defined for an annual batch schedule. The product must be set up in the Meter Characteristics screen or provided in the import file. When batches are created from a schedule, each batch starts and ends at the contract hour set in Meter Characteristics on the day specified in the schedule.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Overrides">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Overrides</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="background-color: #ffffff; display: none;" mc-target-name="Overrides">

If there is a month that should use a different schedule, a separate schedule can be set.

<div class="procedure">

To override a month:

1.  Click the expansion button in the Overrides section of the Liquids tab. A month/year selector and Template option will display.
2.  Select the month and year to override the regular schedule with.
3.  Click the button next to the Template edit box. The Batch Schedule Select screen will appear.
4.  Choose the schedule name from the drop-down and click **Select**. The selected schedule will now display in the Template field.
5.  Click on the expansion button in the Overrides section again. The schedule will be added to the list of Overrides.
6.  Click **Save**.

</div>

If an override is selected for a month that has started, it will not be used to create any batches.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Facilities">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Facilities Sub-Tab</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Facilities">

Use the Facilities tab to define valid facilities for a meter. Facilities can be assigned to batches in the Volume Editor. This can be useful information for downstream accounting systems to be able to match batches to contracts.

A facility may not be assigned to a batch in the Volume Editor if it has not first been added as a valid facility in this section of the Meter Editor.

Facilities are created in the Facility Editor within Settings Manager. Each facility can be set up as a From Facility, a To Facility or both a From Facility and a To Facility to indicate where product is flowing.

</div>

 

</div>
